subject: General Science
title: Respiration

outcomes.text: explain the meaning of respiration in living things,
describe aerobic and anaerobic respiration in living things,
relate the respiratory quotient to the type of substrate and type of respiration in living things,
explain factors affecting respiration in living things,
describe economic importance of anaerobic respiration at home and in industry,
appreciate the significance of respiration in living things.

inquiry_questions: How is aerobic and anaerobic respiration important in a society’s economy?
coreCompetencies:
Communication and collaboration: as the learner discusses with peers the factors affecting energy requirements in human beings.
Learning to learn: as the learner carries out activities to investigate anaerobic respiration in living organisms.
values:
Integrity: as the learner observes ethical behaviour when working on a project of value addition of food products that utilises the concept of aerobic respiration.
Peace: as the learner works harmoniously with others in carrying out a project that utilises the concept of anaerobic respiration such as making of yoghurt, porridge, biogas.
pcis:
Financial literacy: as the learner undertakes a project that utilises the concept of anaerobic respiration in value addition of food products such as milk and flour.
Environmental issues: as the learner develops the skill of making biogas as an alternative source of fuel (energy).
transcription_policy: Source wording retained;line breaks/bullets normalised;source pixels authority.
notes: Source Integrity value says aerobic respiration for food value-addition while its project/other rows say anaerobic;verbatim preserved but actual lactic fermentation teaching is not relabelled aerobic.

RQ=CO2produced/O2consumed;zerooxygen denominator has no finite conventional quotient and cannot alone identify exact substrate/process.
